      "id": "procedure-planning",
      "rationale": "The work package cover showed a blank temporary instruction field and no signed maintenance release at the time of interruption, despite an issued ECP revision. This suggests potential gaps in procedure adherence or planning for boundary acceptance.",

        "4df0cf7c-f4aa-49ea-a08a-ea4cd74d41f2#1: Temporary instruction attachment field: blank... Maintenance release signature: not yet signed at notification time.",

        "If engineering disposition for any service-routing change occurred"
      ],

      "rationale": "The interruption happened while RHOB observed and Utilities prepared, with no confirmed source location or authorized line opening. Coordination between the observing area (RHOB) and preparing team (Utilities) appears critical.",

        "incident-description: ...while a two-person Utilities team was preparing... The initial notification does not establish whether the interruption began at the air source, within the distribution system...",

        "Whether specific communication protocols were followed between Utilities operations (custodian) and RHOB operations",
        "If supervision was present during the critical boundary preparation phase"

      "confidence": 0.80

    {

        "aa0527b9-a6e3-4782-bb4e-b6cc9eb9dbcc#1: Dryer aisle | ...main-route valves M-101/M-102",

      "unknowns": [
        "Which specific valve(s) were open/closed during boundary preparation",
        "Whether LOTO tags were correctly applied to all relevant isolation points"

      "confidence": 0.70

    {
      "id": "equipment-tool",
      "rationale": "The interruption affected the instrument-air supply system (compressor/dryer, headers). While no equipment failure is confirmed yet, the investigation must rule out or confirm mechanical issues with valves M-101/M-102 or header H-R.",

        "incident-description: ...reported loss of instrument-air pressure...",

        "structuredIncident: equipment... Main-route valves M-101/M-102 | status unknown"
      ],
      "unknowns": [
        "Whether a valve failed mechanically or was inadvertently operated",
        "If the compressor/dryer system had known maintenance issues prior to WO-527"
      ],
      "confidence": 0.65
    },
    {
      "id": "other-novel",
      "rationale": "The scenario involves a 'synthetic evaluation record' where the interruption source is explicitly unknown (source vs distribution vs receiving). This may represent a novel condition of intermittent supply loss during boundary preparation that does not fit standard failure modes.",
      "evidence": [
        "incident-description: Synthetic evaluation record derived from a historical incident. Not an actual company record or operating instruction...",
        "structuredIncident: unknowns... Whether the interruption originated at the air source, distribution system, or receiving equipment"
      ],
      "unknowns": [
        "If this represents a unique systemic vulnerability not covered by existing tags",
        "Whether 'synthetic' nature implies hypothetical scenarios that require novel analysis frameworks"
      ],
      "confidence": 0.55
    }

    "summary": "Selected six fixed-taxonomy tags based on evidence linking human actions during boundary preparation, procedural gaps in work package documentation (blank temporary instruction field), communication breakdowns between RHOB and Utilities areas, isolation/LOTO uncertainties regarding valve states M-101/M-102, potential equipment/tool involvement with the instrument-air system, and a novel condition due to unknown interruption origin.
